title: No generic fast-forwarding
locator: Supplementary Note 8, Theorem 5 · arXiv v2, Definition 1 and Theorem 6
scope: Fix c > 1. If one efficient procedure could fast-forward every norm-one, 2-sparse, efficiently row-computable n-qubit Hamiltonian to any time t ≤ 2^(n^(1/c)) with error n^(−4/c), then BQP = PSPACE. The error bounds the vector norm on every input with clean ancillas, relative to ideal evolution with those ancillas returned to zero.

title: Sparse-oracle no-fast-forwarding
scope: For every positive integer N the paper constructs a 2-sparse row-oracle Hamiltonian family with scaled time τ = ‖H‖t = πN/2. A simulator attaining trace-distance precision 1/4 for the family requires at least τ/(2π) = N/4 queries in the worst case.

title: Simultaneous classical-shadow predictions
scope: Fix M Hermitian observables on n qubits and an invertible shadow measurement channel. Use K = ⌈2 log(2M/δ)⌉ independent batches of order 34 maxᵢ‖Oᵢ − Tr(Oᵢ)I/2ⁿ‖²shadow/ε² snapshots each. For 0 < ε,δ < 1 the medians of the batch means are simultaneously within ε of all M expectations with probability at least 1−δ.

title: Quantum memory advantage for predicting observables
locator: Theorem 1 · Supplementary Definition 2 and Theorem 6, Appendix D.1–D.3
scope: Draw a uniform nonidentity Pauli P. With equal probability prepare ρ = I/2ⁿ or ρ = (I + 0.9sP)/2ⁿ for a hidden uniform sign s. P is revealed after acquisition. Estimating |Tr(Pρ)| within 0.25 with success at least 0.8 requires Ω(2ⁿ) copies under adaptive single-copy measurements with classical memory. Joint Bell measurements on pairs of copies suffice with O(1) copies.

title: Window propagation for first-order OTOCs
locator: Theorem 1, Eq. (III.1) · Definition 3, Algorithm 2, Appendix C.4 Theorem 4
scope: For n,d ≥ 2 (even for notation) let U be an open 1D depth-d brickwork circuit of independent Haar U(4) gates. Given its efficient description and 0 < ε < 1, deterministic window propagation estimates 2⁻ⁿ Tr[(U† Xₙ U Z₁)²] with mean-squared error at most ε over U. The polynomial runtime in n, d and 1/ε counts updates of retained coefficients. The source leaves finite-precision gate encoding and bit-cost analysis implicit.

title: Classical simulation at bounded Schmidt rank
scope: In a polynomial-size pure-state computation with one- and two-qubit gates, suppose χ, the maximum Schmidt rank over bipartitions, stays polynomial in n at all steps. Vidal’s tensor representation and gate updates then simulate the computation with polynomial classical time and memory.

title: Adiabatic following without a gap
scope: Let H(s) be a smooth bounded self-adjoint Hamiltonian path with a smooth finite-rank spectral projection P(s). For a state initially in ran P(0), evolution over runtime τ has distance o(1) from ran P(s), uniformly for s ∈ [0,1] as τ → ∞. The theorem needs no uniform spectral gap and supplies no universal rate.

title: Complexity of a generic sign-problem solution
locator: Sign-free comparison and complexity definition, Eqs. (8)–(9) · spin-glass reduction and note [9]
scope: For the constructed quantum spin model, the related sign-free bosonic system has a polynomial-time Monte Carlo method. A generic polynomial-complexity cure for estimating the signed thermal average would decide an NP-complete spin-glass instance in polynomial time with bounded error. Monte Carlo sampling gives the randomized implication NP ⊆ BPP.

title: Amplitude-estimation error guarantee
scope: For success probability a, amplitude estimation Est_Amp(A, χ, M) uses M evaluations of the Boolean success predicate. With probability at least 8/π² its estimate differs from a by at most 2π√(a(1−a))/M + π²/M².

title: Optimality of quantum search
scope: For N equiprobable single-marked-item phase oracles and T queries up to the first Grover maximum, Grover’s average success sin²((2T+1) arcsin(1/√N)) is optimal. To reach success tending to one takes at least (π/4 − o(1))√N oracle calls.

title: Polynomial singular-value transformation
locator: Theorem 17, Eq. (32) · phase admissibility in Corollary 8
scope: Let U be unitary on a finite-dimensional Hilbert space, Π and Π̃ orthogonal projectors, and P a complex degree-d polynomial satisfying Corollary 8’s parity and magnitude conditions. A sequence of d phases and alternating U/U† applications implements the singular-value transform of Π̃UΠ. Its extracted block is Π̃UΦΠ for odd d and ΠUΦΠ for even d.

title: Fixed-basis electronic energy is QMA-complete
scope: Given electron number η, a concisely specified single-particle basis and external potential with efficiently computable integrals, decide E₀ ≤ a versus E₀ ≥ b on the η-electron sector for b−a ≥ 1/poly(η). This promise problem is QMA-complete. The hardness construction uses V = 0 and physical kinetic and Coulomb integrals.

title: Lowest Slater energy is NP-complete
scope: For the same fixed-basis electronic Hamiltonians and electron-number sector, decide whether some single Slater determinant has expected energy ≤ a or every such determinant has energy ≥ b, at inverse-polynomial promise gap. This problem is NP-complete.

title: Fermionic N-representability
locator: Main N-representability promise problem, pp. 1–2 · oracle reduction and QMA verifier
scope: For N fermions in d ≤ poly(N) modes, the input is a two-fermion density matrix ρ and β ≥ 1/poly(N) given to polynomially many bits. Decide exact representability by an N-fermion mixed state versus trace-norm distance at least β from every representable marginal. The problem is QMA-complete under polynomial-time Turing reductions.

title: Five-local Hamiltonian is QMA-complete
locator: Proposition 14.2 and Theorem 14.3 · five-local clock in §14.4.5
scope: Given a sum of polynomially many qubit terms 0 ≤ Hⱼ ≤ I acting on at most five qubits each and thresholds a < b with inverse-polynomial separation, distinguish λmin(H) ≤ a from λmin(H) > b. This promise problem is QMA-complete under polynomial-time Karp reductions. The book calls the witness class BQNP.

title: Single-reference coupled-cluster scaling
locator: Single-reference coupled-cluster discussion at Fig. 3A · Supplementary §§S2.7, S5
scope: Lee et al. propose poly(L)·poly(1/ε) effort for coupled cluster to reach energy error ε on single-reference problems, with L measuring system size. The argument uses empirical excitation-rank convergence for N₂ and extensivity for noninteracting replicas. Uniform input-class, convergence and iteration guarantees remain to be established.
